question: Referee SMALL_DEGREE_FAMILIES.md sections 2.2-2.3 and smallfam/cyclobound.py: is the fibre bound proof and its code correct?
answer: Z_p proof and code match the universal group exactly (psi hom, ball image equal, fibre counts agree on 7 groups, 47 connected graphs sound, unit and admissibility reductions valid). Real gap: squarefree-m remark (md:226-227) unproven since 1-r^j is not a unit (m=15, r=7); also docstring eps_{i-1} (cyclobound.py:6) and bound() cache ignores FIBER (l.155-156).
next: State the squarefree remark with Delta-1 formal slots (as section 2.4) or prove the normal form for composite m; fix the docstring; key bound() cache by FIBER.

question: Referee s.2.4 growth bound and the (3,7) claim: no cubic bipartite diameter-7 graph with more than 168 vertices has a free colour-preserving group with at most 6 vertex orbits. Are the bases, lift logic, group-order ranges and coverage right?
answer: Yes for the (3,7) claim: bases are 1, 1 and 3 classes for m=1,2,3 (checked by enumeration); orders 85-127, 43-63 and 29-42 are exactly the n>168, n<=254 ranges; GAP group counts match every TSV (512, 131, 101 rows); all five files have zero solutions. The s.2.4 bound holds, but the action of Z^(Delta-1) and the homomorphism are unstated (naive action fails 1794/2000 test words, correct action 0/2000). The order-42 2+2 claim in s.2.5 is cited to a file that starts at order 43.
evidence: research/theorems/SMALL_DEGREE_FAMILIES.md:249-253 (s.2.4), :276-285 (s.2.5 (3,7)); smallfam/runs/lift_b22_D7.tsv (orders 43-63; lift_b22.sh); smallfam/runs/allgroups_d3D7.tsv, lift_b33_0_D7.tsv, lift_b33_1_D7.tsv, lift_b33_2_D7_idfix.tsv; squads/r3-smallfam/c4/check_counts.py, nrsg_out.txt, hom_test.py, check_bases_costs.py, notes.md
next: State the action (e_i acts by x^(j_i)) and phi(P,n) = (sum a_i P_i(r), sum n_i j_i) in s.2.4; run or cite order 42 for the 2+2 base; reword the s.2.5 coverage sentence to 168 < n <= 254.

question: Is the §2.3 fibre bound or the §2.4 metacyclic growth bound N <= (2D+1)^((o+1)(Delta-1)) already published (e.g. in Macbeth, Siagiova, Siran 2012)?
answer: Not found in any source I could read. The Macbeth-Siagiova-Siran metacyclic result is UNVERIFIED because ORO and ScienceDirect returned 403 and the abstract was not read. Dougherty-Faber (math/9412223) gives only the Abelian free-Z^d counting bound (Prop. 2, |S_k|), with no metacyclic or non-Abelian content.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9412223 (Prop 2, Thm 11); https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/mathwiki/images/2/21/The_Degree-Diameter_Problem%2C_and_Some_Cayley_Graphs_on_Cyclic_Groups.pdf (1 page, no metacyclic); https://oro.open.ac.uk/30423 (403); https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0012365X1100149X (403); research/squads/r3-smallfam/c1/notes.md
next: Get the 2012 abstract and metacyclic theorem (author copy, library, or MathSciNet MR2852512) and check whether it is an upper bound; if it is only a construction, treat §2.3 and §2.4 as unpublished pending the referee check.

question: Who built the bipartite (3,10) 800 and (3,7) 168 table graphs, and does any post-2012 bipartite (Delta,D) result beat the CombinatoricsWiki bipartite cells (3,7) 168, (3,9) 506, (3,10) 800, (4,8) 2184, (4,9) 4970?
answer: The five cells match the CombinatoricsWiki bipartite table as of 10 Mar 2013 (DS14v2 Table 4). No source read credits 800 or 168 to Delorme-Gomez-Quisquater or Conder-Nedela (Nedela is absent from the survey). No post-2012 bipartite result beats any of the five: the post-2012 bipartite records found are diameter 3, and the 2026 C(k,q) family has degree (q+1)^k and diameter 2k+1, so degree 3 or 4 only at diameter 3. The live wiki returned 503, so the check is against the 2013 snapshot.
evidence: https://www.combinatorics.org/files/Surveys/ds14/ds14v2-2013.pdf (Table 4 p.37; s.3.4.4-3.4.5; refs [50],[64],[118],[119],[127],[152],[240]); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.27253 (Thm 1.1, Thm 6.11, ref [34]); https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3588; https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.02427; https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.3190090304; https://web.mat.upc.edu/francesc.comellas/old-files/nlarge/nlarge_f.pdf; research/squads/r3-smallfam/c2/notes.md
next: Re-read the live CombinatoricsWiki bipartite table (503 here) for current cell values and sources, then read Delorme 1985 (JGT 9:325-334) and Cames van Batenburg-Korsky arXiv:2608.03965 for the (3,10) and (3,7) constructions.
